extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in Alan Moore, comics history, and creative-practice of graphic-novel authors
extracted.subtask_description: Practices, thematic choices, and production decisions illustrated by Alan Moore's career that serve as evaluative criteria or guidance for writing and producing comics and graphic novels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity reset / character amnesia
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking over existing serials Moore used the "familiar tactic of wiping out what had gone before, giving the hero amnesia and revealing that everything we'd learned to that point was a lie."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a continuity reset (amnesia, retcon) as a strategy to start afresh with a character and avoid being constrained by earlier canon. Example: Moore's approach on Marvelman, Swamp Thing, Supreme. Anti-pattern: leaving yourself constrained by past continuity, limiting creative options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply literary sensibilities and adult/challenging themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore "applies literary sensibilities to the mainstream of the medium as well as including challenging subject matter and adult themes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate literary techniques, complex themes, and mature subject matter into comics to elevate mainstream work. Example: Watchmen and From Hell. Scoring note: strength is judged by sophistication of theme integration and how well literary devices enrich the comic format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit comics-specific affordances ('design to be un-filmable')
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore wanted to "concentrate on those things that only comics could achieve" and said much of his work "was designed to be un-filmable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft narratives that leverage visual density, panel-to-panel juxtaposition, and text-image dissonance unique to comics. Concrete tactics: pack information visually in panels, use juxtaposition between what is said and what is shown. Anti-pattern: writing as if the comic is just a film script, losing comic-specific techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intertextuality and use of literary characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Victorian literary characters and wide literary references (e.g., The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen featured Allan Quatermain, Invisible Man, Captain Nemo, Dr. Jekyll and Mr Hyde, Wilhelmina Murray).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ intertextual casting and literary pastiche to create layered meaning and appeal to readers' literary knowledge. Example: pitting the League against Professor Moriarty or Martians from The War of the Worlds. Consider rights/public-domain issues and how pastiche contributes to theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period pastiche and stylistic pastiches
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore wrote stories in period styles and used pastiche (e.g., Tom Strong flashbacks in period styles; Supreme based on Silver Age Superman comics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt historical or genre-specific stylistic modes (language, artwork conventions, narrative voice) to evoke eras and comment on the medium's history. Use pastiche to create tone and meta-commentary. Scoring: authenticity and purposiveness of the pastiche.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive worldbuilding / fabricated history
rubrics_metrics.description: He "created a long and distinguished history for these new characters, retro-fitting a fake silver and gold age for them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct deep, retroactive histories (fake ages, invented backstories) to give characters mythic weight and a sense of cultural depth. Example: Awesome Universe backstory. Anti-pattern: shallow or contradictory retro-history that undermines suspension of disbelief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of occult/esoteric/philosophical systems as narrative structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Works like Promethea explored occult themes, particularly the Qabalah, and used the Kabbalistic tree of life as a structural device; Moore sees magic and writing as linked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured esoteric or philosophical systems (e.g., Qabalah, tarot, 'Idea Space') as organizing devices for plot and theme. Example: Promethea explicitly uses Kabbalistic structures. Consider clarity for readers and how personal belief systems inform fiction; can make work highly personal and dense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthology format to showcase variety and revive forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Tomorrow Stories was notable as an anthology series featuring a regular cast of varied characters, reviving a medium that had largely died out in American comics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anthology formats to present diverse tones, experiment with form, and provide space for different creators/characters within one publication. Benefit: showcases range and can revive or sustain traditions; drawback: less continuity for single-character readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-blending (mixing conventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Top 10 is a deadpan police procedural drama set in a superhero city where everyone has super-powers and secret identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blend disparate genres (e.g., police procedural + superhero) to create novel narrative frameworks and fresh thematic angles. Evaluate by how smoothly conventions are integrated and whether the hybrid produces new insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curate collaborators and write detailed scripts to leverage artists
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore's "hyper detailed scripts always play to the strengths of the artists he works with." He lined up artists and writers for his imprint and curated teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act as a curator: choose collaborators whose skills fit the story and provide detailed scripting to enable visual storytelling. Practical guidance: match artist strengths to required visual styles, provide specifics in script while leaving room for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize innovation over pandering to fan expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore admitted at times he had catered "too much to his conceptions of what the fans wanted rather than being innovative," expressing dissatisfaction with that approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor creative risk and innovation rather than tailoring work solely to perceived fan desires. Anti-pattern: excessive catering that leads to formulaic or less original work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary accessibility and subtlety according to aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Tom Strong was described as "more subtle" and "ABC's most accessible comic," while other works are denser and more experimental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately calibrate level of accessibility—some projects aim for broad readability, others for experimental subtlety. Evaluate based on target audience fit and effectiveness of chosen complexity level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mythic and archetypal elements to restore heroic resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: With Supreme Moore harked back to the original "mythic" figure of the American superhero, introducing archetypal figures (Suprema, Radar, Supremium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ archetypes and mythic motifs to evoke classic heroic resonance and to comment on genre conventions. Scoring: how effectively archetypal elements serve both homage and critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect authorial integrity and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore insisted on removing his name from adaptations he did not own and refused to be associated with adaptations that altered his work, expressing preference not to accept money from such adaptations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain control over how your work is adapted and protect moral/creative rights; negotiate ownership and credits carefully. This is both an ethical/production criterion and a practice for sustaining artistic integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment with platforms, formats, and interactive tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Moore led projects such as Dodgem Logic (a bi-monthly magazine) and Electricomics (an open source app for reading and creating interactive comics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore new publication platforms and interactive formats to expand how stories are created and consumed. Evaluate experiments on innovation, accessibility, and whether they extend the storytelling possibilities of the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infuse personal belief systems and 'personal statement' into work
rubrics_metrics.description: Promethea has been described as "a personal statement" encompassing "a belief system, a personal cosmology."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use personal philosophy and worldview as a source of thematic coherence and emotional weight. Risk: extremely personal works may alienate some readers; reward: can produce deeply resonant, distinctive narratives.
